best.plan_strategy: Attempt 2 spends the whole attempt on the ranking axis by swapping to a different boosted family with a markedly different regularisation regime: xgboost with shallow-but-numerous trees, row and column subsampling, and a low learning rate, fitted under the same NaN-native pipeline (impute: none, no scaling) so the categoricals' missing branch is still learned directly. The operating point is set once with scale_pos_weight = 3.18 (the card's imbalance ratio), which is where balanced_accuracy's recall/specificity crossover sits; cut_headroom 0.0057 from attempt 1 says nothing more is available on that axis, so no further weight search is planned. Add the single missing_count column — the one missingness feature a NaN-splitting family cannot already express, aggregating across workclass/occupation/native-country non-response — as the only feature-side change; missing_indicator is deliberately not used because it is bit-for-bit redundant under impute: none. early_stopping_rounds=60 lets the executor hold its own 10% stopping slice back so the 1200 low-rate rounds do not run past the point where the ordering stops improving (attempt 1's train_val_gap 0.0862 shows the previous configuration was buying train-only structure). After the fit I will read roc_auc / pr_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against attempt 1's 0.9260 / 0.8259 / 0.8464: if the ceiling moves less than ~0.005 then the boosted-tree ranking on these 14 columns is saturated well below the 0.8364 KS the bar requires, and the remaining attempts should test a structurally different ranking generator (extra_trees/random_forest bagging, or mlp on a scaled imputed matrix) rather than another point in gbdt space.

critic.evidence: Attempt 1 (hist_gbdt, class_weight='balanced') scored balanced_accuracy=0.8407 (95% CI 0.8325~0.8498) against the bar 0.9182 — a shortfall of 0.0775. The operating point is already spent: recall 0.8310 vs specificity 0.8505 are nearly equal, and cut_headroom is only 0.005654 (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8464), i.e. the best cut of this ranking buys at most 7% of the remaining 0.0775; the other 93% is ranking. The ranking itself is roc_auc 0.9260, pr_auc 0.8259, implied KS = 2*0.8464-1 = 0.6928 versus the required KS 0.8364 — still 0.1436 short even though this family already lifted the ceiling from the baseline's 0.8238 to 0.8464. train_val_gap is 0.0862 (train balanced_accuracy 0.9269 vs val 0.8407), so extra capacity is not the lever either — capacity is already being spent on train-only structure with max_leaf_nodes=63 / max_iter=500 / no early stopping. No dropped_hyperparams, no error, 18.45 s of a 600 s budget, so nothing was resource-limited. Only one family has been tried (span of ranking ceilings across families here is 0.0022–0.0077 roc_auc, far under the 0.0775 gap), so a plain family swap alone is not a plan that reaches the bar; the one untried ranking lever the executor still allows is a differently-regularised boosted family plus the missing_count column (missing_indicator is bit-for-bit redundant under impute: none and must not be spent).
critic.direction: Spend the next attempt on the ranking axis, not the cut: fit xgboost with markedly different regularisation (shallower trees, subsampling, column subsampling, more rounds at a lower learning rate) under the same impute: none pipeline and scale_pos_weight at the class ratio, since cut_headroom 0.0057 proves the threshold/weight lever is exhausted and the 0.0862 train_val_gap says the current 63-leaf hist_gbdt is spending capacity on noise rather than on a better ordering.

critic.evidence: Attempt 2 (xgboost, scale_pos_weight 3.18, missing_count on) scored balanced_accuracy 0.8467 (95% CI 0.8391~0.8550) against the bar 0.9182 — still 0.0715 short. The paired Δ vs iteration 1 is +0.0060 (CI +0.0010~+0.0115, P 0.988), so the move is real but tiny, and that row moved family AND preprocessing together (missing_count false→true), so neither lever owns it. The operating point is finished: recall 0.8567 vs specificity 0.8368 are within 0.020 of each other and cut_headroom is 0.00278 — 4% of the remaining 0.0715; the other 96% is ranking. The ranking itself barely moved: roc_auc 0.9260→0.9293, pr_auc 0.8259→0.8296, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.8464→0.8495, implied KS 0.6990 versus the required 0.8364 — 0.1374 short. The spread of ranking ceilings across the two families tried is only 0.0031 (0.8464~0.8495) while the distance from the best cut to the bar is 0.0687, i.e. 22× that span, so one more boosted/tree family off the same list cannot reach 0.9182. Capacity is no longer the issue either (train_val_gap fell 0.0862→0.0285, train balanced_accuracy 0.8752 vs val 0.8467, stopped_at_iter 1198/1200), nothing was dropped (dropped_hyperparams empty), and 12.8 s of a 600 s budget was used, so no resource limit. With 3 iterations left the honest reading is that the bar sits above what any threshold of any ranking these 14 columns have produced permits, and the executor cannot derive new features.
critic.direction: Spend the next attempt on a structurally different ranking generator rather than another point in boosted-tree space — fit a bagged, fully-grown extra_trees with balanced class weight under the same impute: none-equivalent pipeline (median impute is forced for that family) and change nothing else, so the row is attributable — and read balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut / roc_auc: if the ceiling again moves under ~0.005 the ranking on these 14 columns is saturated ~0.069 below the bar and the run should report 0.9182 as unreachable with the available levers.

critic.evidence: Attempt 3 (extra_trees, 800 trees, min_samples_leaf=2, class_weight='balanced', median impute) scored balanced_accuracy 0.8134 (95% CI 0.8054~0.8211) against the bar 0.9182 — 0.1048 short, and the paired Δ vs the best (iteration 2, 0.8467) is -0.0333 (CI -0.0404~-0.0269, P(improve) 0.000), a resolved regression. That row also moved impute none→median with the family, so it has two owners and is not evidence about either lever alone. Nothing was resource-limited (8.4 s of 600 s, returncode 0, dropped_hyperparams empty). The operating point is spent in every attempt: cut_headroom 0.005654 → 0.00278 → 0.0039, and this attempt's 0.0039 is 4% of the 0.1048 still to go, with recall 0.8323 vs specificity 0.7945 within 0.038 — so 96% of the shortfall is on the ranking axis. But the ranking axis is where the family swaps have already been priced: across the three families tried, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut spans only 0.8173~0.8495 (width 0.0322, and that is a range over per-family maxima, not a paired test), while the distance from the best cut 0.8495 to the bar is 0.0687 — 2× that span. In KS terms the bar needs 0.8364 and the best ranking so far implies 0.6990, i.e. 0.1374 short. Capacity is not the lever either: this attempt's train balanced_accuracy 0.8737 vs val 0.8134 gives train_val_gap 0.0603, and iteration 2's gap was already down to 0.0285 with train 0.8752 — both trains sit ~0.07–0.10 below the 0.9182 bar, so the fitted models cannot reach it even on the rows they saw. With the executor unable to derive features, two wrong_model_family prescriptions having bought +0.0060 then -0.0333, and 2 iterations left, the bar is above what any threshold of any ranking these 14 columns have produced permits.
critic.direction: Stop spending iterations on more tree families — the swap span (0.0322) is half the remaining ranking gap (0.0687) — and instead make the single largest untried structural move on the ranking axis with an attributable row: refit the exact iteration-2 xgboost configuration but with more capacity per tree (deeper trees, weaker shrinkage-per-tree constraints) under the identical impute: none / missing_count: true pipeline, since iteration 2's train balanced_accuracy 0.8752 with gap 0.0285 shows the booster is capacity-limited rather than overfit, and if that ranking again moves under ~0.005 the run should report 0.9182 as unreachable with the executor's levers.
